It sounds incredibly unsettling to be in a situation where you feel unsure of what is actually happening in your own home. When someone appears to be having full conversations with someone who isn't there, it generally points to two very different possibilities. He could genuinely be experiencing a mental health issue, such as auditory hallucinations, or he might just have an intense habit of vocalizing his thoughts. However, if you feel he is deliberately trying to confuse you or make you doubt your reality, that is a form of emotional manipulation often called gaslighting.

Because both scenarios are deeply concerning, it is important to prioritize your own well-being. You might find it helpful to speak privately with a counselor or therapist. A professional can help you sort through your observations, trust your instincts, and figure out the healthiest next steps for yourself, regardless of what is actually causing his behavior.
